concepts.title: for loops
concepts.summary: `for x in things:` runs the indented lines once for each item, with `x` set to that item.

concepts.title: len()
concepts.summary: `len(s)` is how many items `s` holds: characters in a string, entries in a list.

concepts.title: .lower()
concepts.summary: `s.lower()` is a copy of `s` in small letters.

concepts.title: .count()
concepts.summary: `s.count(x)` is how many times `x` appears in `s`.

concepts.title: f-strings
concepts.summary: `f"{n} letters"` puts the value of `n` into the text.

cells.text: A sentence is just a string of characters, and Python can count them. Run the cell below, then change the sentence and run it again.

cells.label: Count the characters
cells.text:
sentence = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
print(len(sentence), "characters")

cells.question: What will this print?
cells.explain: `count` looks for every `a` in `banana`: there are three.

cells.text:
### Your turn

Capital and small letters are different characters to Python, so `"T"` and `"t"` are counted apart. Small letters first, then count.

cells.task: Make `n` the number of times the letter **t** appears in `sentence`, whether it is written `T` or `t`.
cells.text:
sentence = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
n = 0  # change this line
print(n)
cells.check: assert n == sentence.lower().count("t"), "n should count both T and t. Try making the sentence small letters first."
hints: `sentence.lower()` is the sentence in small letters.
`sentence.lower().count("t")` counts the small t's of that copy.
cells.solution:
sentence = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
n = sentence.lower().count("t")
print(n)

cells.task: Print how many times each letter of the alphabet appears, one line per letter that appears at least once, like `e 3`.
cells.text:
sentence = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
# your loop here
cells.check:
assert "o 4" in _printed, "The line for o should say 4."
assert "e 3" in _printed, "The line for e should say 3."
cells.hint: `for letter in alphabet:` visits each letter; inside, count it in `sentence.lower()` and print it with an f-string when the count is more than 0.
